metadata.title: Finite generation conjectures for cohomology over finite fields

extraction_notes.note: The introduction's numbered diagram (1) (label less) is the same diagram as (maind) in Proposition 3.2; both are numbered environments, so I kept the body copy EP9 and gave the introduction copy no node, as the restated-copy rule says. No node contains the intro's \eqref{less}, so no edge is lost.

Introduction statements that Section 2-3 repeat formally (Frobenius and Kato cohomology, H^{2n}_K = CH^n(\bar X)_G, the vanishing under Parshin, Pirutka's example) get no node. The motivational equivalences around Bass' conjecture also get none.

Pirutka's example is described twice and the two disagree: the introduction says a geometrically rational surface, Section 3.1 says a geometrically birational variety of dimension 5. I kept the Section 3.1 sentence.

The lead-in phrases 'Since ... we have' and 'As in Proposition \ref{ssprop}, we obtain' run straight into the lemma or proposition environment without ending the sentence. I emitted each as a one-sentence prose proof.

The Section 3.2 discussion derives diagrams under Parshin's conjecture and concludes that Kato homology measures the failure of integral Tate; it states no separate claim, so I kept it as one remark (with its two numbered diagrams nested) rather than as a claim with a proof.
These are the author's own earlier results ('we showed in \cite{...}'), stated here without proof, so they are marked external with the earlier paper as citation.

nodes.name: Bass' conjecture
nodes.statement: Bass conjectured that for a regular scheme $X$ of finite type over the integers, the higher algebraic $K$-groups are finitely generated \cite{bassln342}.
nodes.statement_short: Higher algebraic K-groups of regular schemes of finite type over Z are finitely generated.
assumptions: for a regular scheme $X$ of finite type over the integers
conclusions: the higher algebraic $K$-groups are finitely generated

nodes.name: Weil-etale cohomology
nodes.statement: Still for $X$ of finite type over a finite field, LIchtenbaum's Weil-etale cohomology $H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is defined as the cohomology of $R\Gamma_GR\Gamma_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$, where $G$ is the Weil-group of the finite field.
nodes.statement_short: Lichtenbaum's Weil-etale cohomology: cohomology of $R\Gamma_G R\Gamma_{et}(\bar X,\mathbb Z(n))$ for the Weil group $G$.

nodes.name: Finite generation of Weil-etale cohomology vs Tate and Beilinson conjectures
nodes.statement: Using ideas of Kahn, we showed in \cite{ichweilI} that the finite generation of $H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ for smooth and proper $X$ is equivalent to the strong form of Tate's and Beilinson's conjecture.
nodes.statement_short: For smooth proper X, finite generation of Weil-etale cohomology is equivalent to the strong Tate and Beilinson conjectures.
conclusions:
is equivalent to the strong form of Tate's and 
Beilinson's conjecture

nodes.name: Geometric Frobenius and Weil group
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi$ be the geometric Frobenius, and $G=\langle \varphi\rangle$ be the Weil group of ${{\mathbb F}}_q$.

nodes.name: Bloch's cycle complex ${{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)$
nodes.statement: Let ${{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)$ be the cycle complex defined by Bloch shifted by $2n$, so that $$H_i({{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(X)) = CH_n(X,i-2n).$$
nodes.genus: the cycle complex defined by Bloch

nodes.name: Higher Chow groups agree with motivic cohomology
nodes.statement: This agrees with motivic cohomology $H^{2d-i}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(d-n))$ for smooth $X$ of pure dimension $d$ by \cite{voevodsky}.
nodes.statement_short: Homology of the shifted cycle complex agrees with motivic cohomology for smooth X.
conclusions:
This agrees with motivic cohomology 
$H^{2d-i}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(d-n))$

nodes.name: Frobenius homology and Kato homology
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be an abelian group. \begin{enumerate} \item We define $H_i^c(X,A(n))$ to be $H_i({{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(X)\otimes A)$. \item We define Frobenius homology $H_i^F(X,A(n))$ to be the homology of the double complex $$ {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A \xrightarrow{\varphi-1} {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A.$$ Here $\varphi$ acts covariantly in $\bar X$ on cycles on $\bar X\times \Delta^i$; the left and right hand complexes sit in homological degrees $1$ and $0$, respectively. \item The Kato homology $H_i^K(X,A(n))$ is defined to be the homology of the complex of coinvariants $\big({{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Define $H^c$ as homology of the cycle complex, Frobenius homology via the cone of $\varphi-1$, Kato homology via $G$-coinvariants.
nodes.label: def1

nodes.name: Frobenius homology with finite coefficients is Galois cohomology
nodes.statement: Note that $H_i^F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))$ is isomorphic to $H^{1-i}(Gal({{\mathbb F}}_q),{{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n)(\bar X))$ because with torsion coefficients, Galois cohomology can be calculated by the complex above.
nodes.statement_short: With $\mathbb Z/m$ coefficients, Frobenius homology is Galois cohomology of the cycle complex over $\bar X$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: The following lemma follows from the definitions.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the definitions.

nodes.name: Vanishing and descent sequences for Frobenius and Kato homology
nodes.statement: The groups $H_i^c(X,A(n))$, $H_i^F(X,A(n))$ and $H_i^K(X,A(n))$ vanish for $i<2n$. We have $H_{2n}^c(X,A(n))\cong CH_n(X)\otimes A$ and $$H_{2n}^K(X,A(n))\cong H_{2n}^F(X,A(n)) \cong \big( CH_n(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G.$$ For all $i$, there are short exact sequences \begin{equation} 0\to H_i^c(\bar X,A(n))_G\to H_i^F(X,A(n))\to H_{i-1}^c(\bar X,A(n))^G \to 0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The three homologies vanish below $2n$, compute Chow groups in degree $2n$, and Frobenius homology sits in descent short exact sequences.
conclusions:
The groups $H_i^c(X,A(n))$, $H_i^F(X,A(n))$ and $H_i^K(X,A(n))$ 
vanish for $i<2n$.
nodes.label: lem1

nodes.name: Frobenius descent short exact sequence
nodes.statement: 0\to H_i^c(\bar X,A(n))_G\to H_i^F(X,A(n))\to H_{i-1}^c(\bar X,A(n))^G \to 0.
nodes.label: yyy

nodes.name: Long exact sequence relating cycle, Frobenius and Kato homology
nodes.statement: We have an exact sequence \begin{equation} \cdots\to H_i^c(X,A(n)) \to H_{i+1}^F(X,A(n))\to H_{i+1}^K(X,A(n)) \to H_{i-1}^c(X,A(n)) \to \cdots \end{equation} All three theories are covariently functorial for proper maps, contravariantly functorial for quasi-finite flat maps, and have localization long exact sequences.
nodes.statement_short: Long exact sequence $H^c\to H^F\to H^K$; all three theories have functoriality and localization sequences.
conclusions:
All three theories are covariently functorial for proper maps,
contravariantly functorial for quasi-finite flat maps,
and have localization long exact sequences.
nodes.label: prop1

nodes.name: Long exact sequence (homd)
nodes.statement: \cdots\to H_i^c(X,A(n)) \to H_{i+1}^F(X,A(n))\to H_{i+1}^K(X,A(n)) \to H_{i-1}^c(X,A(n)) \to \cdots
nodes.label: homd

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.3
nodes.statement: This comes from the short exact sequence of double complexes $$\begin{CD} \big( {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)^G@>>> {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A@>>> 0 \\ @VVV @V\varphi-1 VV@VVV \\ 0@>>> {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A @>>> \big({{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G \end{CD}$$ and ${{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(X)\otimes A\cong \big({{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)^G$. Functoriality and the localization property are well-known for cycle complexes, and this carries over to $\big( {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G$ by an easy diagram chase.
nodes.statement_short: Short exact sequence of double complexes plus $\mathbb Z^c(n)(X)\cong(\mathbb Z^c(n)(\bar X))^G$; functoriality by diagram chase.

nodes.name: Frobenius cohomology of a finitely generated field
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated field $K$ of transcendence degree $d$ over ${{\mathbb F}}_q$, define $H^i_F(K,A(j))$ to be $\operatornamewithlimits{colim} H_{2d+1-i}^F(U,A(d-j))$, where $U$ runs through smooth schemes with function field $K$.

nodes.name: Frobenius descent sequence for fields
nodes.statement: 0\to H^{s-t-1}_{\mathcal M}(K\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q,A(s-n))_G \to H^{s-t}_F(K,A(s-n))\to \\ H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(K\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q,A(s-n))^G\to 0,
nodes.label: frobdescent

nodes.name: Niveau spectral sequences
nodes.statement: We have functorial spectral sequences \begin{align*} E^1_{s,t}=\bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k(x),A(s-n))&\Rightarrow H_{s+t}^c(X,A(n));\\ \bar E^1_{s,t}=\bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-t}_F(k(x),A(s-n))&\Rightarrow H_{s+t+1}^F(X,A(n)).\\ \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Coniveau spectral sequences from motivic / Frobenius cohomology of points to cycle and Frobenius homology.
nodes.label: ssprop

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.4
nodes.statement: This follows with the niveau filtration, together with the fact that $$H_{s+t}^c(K,A(n)):= \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{U} H_{s+t}^c(U,A(n)) \cong H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(K,A(s-n))$$ and $H_{s+t+1}^F(K,A(n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(K,A(s-n))$ for a field $K$ of transcendence degree $s$ over the base field.
nodes.statement_short: Niveau filtration, with the identification of homology of a field with its motivic / Frobenius cohomology.

nodes.name: Finite generation conjecture for Borel-Moore homologies
nodes.statement: The groups $H_i^c(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$, $H_{i}^F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ and $H_{i}^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ are finitely generated for any $i, n$ and $X$.
conclusions: are finitely generated for any $i, n$ and $X$.
nodes.label: mainhom

nodes.name: Reduction to smooth proper X
nodes.statement: By localization, it suffices to consider the case of smooth and proper $X$ (assuming that every finitely generated field over ${{\mathbb F}}_q$ has a smooth and proper model).

nodes.name: Parshin's conjecture $P_n$
nodes.statement: Recall from \cite{ichparshin} Parshin's conjecture $P_n$, stating that $CH_n(X,i)$ is torsion for $i\not=0$ and $X$ smooth and projective.
conclusions: $CH_n(X,i)$ is torsion for $i\not=0$

nodes.name: Motivic vs Frobenius cohomology of fields under Parshin
nodes.statement: Assume Conjecture $P_n$. Then $$H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))$$ for $t\geq n$. For $t=n-1$, the left hand side vanishes, and $H^{s-n+1}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))\cong K_{s-n}^M(k\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q)_G$. For $t<n-1$, both sides vanish.
nodes.statement_short: Under $P_n$, motivic and Frobenius cohomology of a field agree for $t\ge n$; for $t=n-1$ Frobenius cohomology is coinvariant Milnor K-theory.
conclusions: For $t<n-1$, both sides vanish.
nodes.label: pupl

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.6
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that the second map and the composition $$H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))\to H^{s-t}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n)) \to H^{s-t}_{\text{\rm et}}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))$$ are isomorphism for $t\geq n$. The total composition is an isomorphism for $t\geq n-1$ by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures. For the second map, we compare \eqref{frobdescent} to the analog short exact sequence for etale cohomology. By Parshin's conjecture, the groups $H^i_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))$ are torsion for $i<s-n$, so that Galois cohomology and cohomology of the Weil-group $G$ agree for those groups. The result now follows with the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures by comparing \eqref{frobdescent} with the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence for Galois cohomology (for the finite product of fields $k\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q$).
nodes.statement_short: Compare Frobenius descent with Hochschild-Serre via Beilinson-Lichtenbaum; Parshin makes Galois and Weil-group cohomology agree.

nodes.name: Reduce to two maps
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that the second map and the composition $$H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))\to H^{s-t}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n)) \to H^{s-t}_{\text{\rm et}}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))$$ are isomorphism for $t\geq n$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to showing the second map and the composition are isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Beilinson-Lichtenbaum for composition
nodes.statement: The total composition is an isomorphism for $t\geq n-1$ by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures.
nodes.statement_short: The composition is an isomorphism by Beilinson-Lichtenbaum.

nodes.name: Compare descent sequences under Parshin
nodes.statement: For the second map, we compare \eqref{frobdescent} to the analog short exact sequence for etale cohomology. By Parshin's conjecture, the groups $H^i_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))$ are torsion for $i<s-n$, so that Galois cohomology and cohomology of the Weil-group $G$ agree for those groups.
nodes.statement_short: Compare Frobenius and Galois descent; Parshin makes Weil-group and Galois cohomology agree.

nodes.name: Conclude via Hochschild-Serre
nodes.statement: The result now follows with the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures by comparing \eqref{frobdescent} with the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence for Galois cohomology (for the finite product of fields $k\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q$).
nodes.statement_short: Conclude with Beilinson-Lichtenbaum and Hochschild-Serre.

nodes.name: Kato complex
nodes.statement: We define the Kato complex $KC_n(X)$ of weight $n$ to be the complex $$ \bigoplus_{X_{(n)}} {{\mathbb Z}} \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(n+1)}} (k(x)\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q)^\times_G \gets \cdots\gets \bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} K_{s-n}^M(k(x)\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q)_G \gets\cdots,$$ with the summand indexed by $X_{(s)}$ in degree $s-n$. The differentials are induced by boundary maps of higher Chow groups of discrete valuation rings.
nodes.statement_short: Complex of coinvariant Milnor K-groups of residue fields over $\bar{\mathbb F}_q$, with boundary-map differentials.

nodes.name: Kato homology is homology of the Kato complex
nodes.statement: Assuming conjecture $P_n$, we have $$H_i^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\cong H_{i-2n}(KC_n(X)).$$ In particular, $H_i^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ vanishes unless $2n\leq i\leq n+d$.
conclusions: $$H_i^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\cong H_{i-2n}(KC_n(X)).$$

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.8
nodes.statement: Compare the spectral sequences of Proposition \ref{ssprop} and use Proposition \ref{pupl}.
nodes.statement_short: Compare the two niveau spectral sequences using Proposition 2.6.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence with finite coefficients
nodes.statement: \cdots\to H_i^c(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n)) \stackrel{\alpha}{\to} H_{i+1}^F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n)) \stackrel{\beta}{\to} H_{i+1}^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))\to \cdots
nodes.label: hommodm

nodes.name: Finiteness conjecture with finite coefficients
nodes.statement: All terms in the \eqref{hommodm} are finite for all $i, n, X$.
conclusions: All terms in the \eqref{hommodm} are finite
nodes.label: finitehom

nodes.name: Structure map $f$
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to {{\mathbb F}}_q$ be the structure map.

nodes.name: Borel-Moore etale homology
nodes.statement: For $p\not|m$ we define $H^{\text{\rm et}}_i(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))$ as the (Borel-Moore) etale homology $H^{-i}(X_{\text{\rm et}},Rf^!\mu_m^{\otimes -n})= H^{-i}(Gal({{\mathbb F}}_q),R\Gamma_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X, Rf^!\mu_m^{\otimes -n}))$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.11
nodes.statement: Since $Gal({{\mathbb F}}_q)$ has cohomological dimension $1$ and $Rf^!\mu_m^{\otimes -n}$ is concentrated in negative degrees, we have
nodes.statement_short: Galois group of a finite field has cohomological dimension 1 and $Rf^!$ is in negative degrees.

nodes.name: Vanishing of etale homology in low degrees
nodes.statement: The groups $H^{\text{\rm et}}_i(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))$ vanish for $i<-1$.
conclusions: The groups $H^{\text{\rm et}}_i(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))$ vanish for $i<-1$.

nodes.name: Notation ${{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n)$
nodes.statement: Writing ${{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n)$ for ${{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)\otimes {{\mathbb Z}}/m$, we showed in \cite{ichduality}:

nodes.name: Duality via cycle complexes
nodes.statement: We have $Rf^!{{\mathbb Z}}/m \cong {{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(0)$ for any $m$. In particular $H^{\text{\rm et}}_i(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))$ agrees with the $-i$th etale hypercohomology of ${{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n)$ if $p\not|m$ and $n\leq 0$.
conclusions: We have $Rf^!{{\mathbb Z}}/m \cong {{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(0)$ for any $m$.
nodes.label: dduuaall

nodes.name: Cap-product map to $Rf^!\mu_m^{\otimes -n}$
nodes.statement: If $p\not| m$ and $k$ contains the $m$-th roots of unity, then cap-product with ${{\mathbb Z}}/m(1)(k)\cong \mu_m(k)$, defines a map $f^*\mu_m\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n)\to {{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n-1)$ of complexes of sheaves on $X/k$, inducing a map $$ {{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n)\to f^*\mu^{\otimes -n}_m\otimes {{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(0) \cong f^* \mu^{\otimes -n}_m\otimes Rf^!Z/m \cong Rf^!\mu^{\otimes -n}_m.$$
nodes.statement_short: Cap product with $\mu_m$ gives a comparison map from the cycle complex mod m to $Rf^!\mu_m^{\otimes -n}$.

nodes.name: The comparison map is not an isomorphism for $n>0$
nodes.statement: This map is in general not an isomorphism for $n>0$; for example, the left hand side vanishes for $n>\dim X$, but the right hand side is periodic in $n$.

nodes.name: Cycle map $\gamma$ from Frobenius homology to etale homology
nodes.statement: This construction induces a a map $$ {{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n)(\bar X) \to R\Gamma_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X, {{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n))\to R\Gamma_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,Rf^!\mu^{\otimes -n}),$$ hence $$\gamma: H_{i+1}^F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))\to H_i^{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))$$ by taking the cone of $\varphi-1$.
nodes.statement_short: The comparison map induces $\gamma: H^F_{i+1}(X,\mathbb Z/m(n))\to H^{et}_i(X,\mathbb Z/m(n))$.

nodes.name: Finiteness for n=0
nodes.statement: Let $n=0$. Then Conjecture \ref{finitehom} holds for $p\not| m$, and for any $m$ under resolution of singularities.
conclusions:
Conjecture \ref{finitehom} holds for $p\not| m$, and for any $m$
under resolution of singularities.
nodes.label: KJS

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.13
nodes.statement: If $n=0$, then $\gamma$ is an isomorphism by \cite{ichduality}, hence Frobenius homology is finite. But by Jannsen-Kerz-Saito \cite{kerzsaito}, Kato homology is finite. If $m=p^r$, then Kato homology is finite under resolution of singularities. To show finiteness of Frobenius homology, one reduces by the usual devissage to the case that $X$ is smooth and proper of dimension $d$. In this case, $\gamma$ is an isomorphic to the finite group $H^{d-i}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\nu^{d}_r)$ by Theorem \ref{dduuaall} and the isomorphism ${{\mathbb Z}}^c/p^r(0) \cong \nu^d_r[d]$.
nodes.statement_short: Case split on $p\nmid m$ (duality and Jannsen-Kerz-Saito) and $m=p^r$ (devissage to smooth proper, Theorem 2.12).

nodes.name: Case p not dividing m
nodes.statement: If $n=0$, then $\gamma$ is an isomorphism by \cite{ichduality}, hence Frobenius homology is finite. But by Jannsen-Kerz-Saito \cite{kerzsaito}, Kato homology is finite.
nodes.statement_short: For $p\nmid m$: duality gives finite Frobenius homology, Jannsen-Kerz-Saito gives finite Kato homology.

nodes.name: Case m = p^r, Kato homology
nodes.statement: If $m=p^r$, then Kato homology is finite under resolution of singularities.
nodes.statement_short: For $m=p^r$, Kato homology is finite under resolution of singularities.

nodes.name: Devissage
nodes.statement: To show finiteness of Frobenius homology, one reduces by the usual devissage to the case that $X$ is smooth and proper of dimension $d$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce by devissage to smooth proper X.

nodes.name: Identify with logarithmic de Rham-Witt cohomology
nodes.statement: In this case, $\gamma$ is an isomorphic to the finite group $H^{d-i}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\nu^{d}_r)$ by Theorem \ref{dduuaall} and the isomorphism ${{\mathbb Z}}^c/p^r(0) \cong \nu^d_r[d]$.
nodes.statement_short: Use Theorem 2.12 to identify with finite etale cohomology of $\nu^d_r$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.14
nodes.statement: As in Proposition \ref{ssprop}, we obtain
nodes.statement_short: Same niveau argument as Proposition 2.4.

nodes.name: Etale niveau spectral sequence
nodes.statement: For $p\not| m$ we have a spectral sequence \begin{equation} \tilde E^1_{s,t}=\bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-t}_{\text{\rm et}}(k(x),\mu_m^{\otimes s-n}) \Rightarrow H_{s+t}^{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n)) \end{equation} The $\tilde E^1$-terms lie in short exact sequences \begin{multline} 0\to H^{s-t-1}_{\text{\rm et}}(k(x)\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n})_G \to H^{s-t}_{\text{\rm et}}(k(x),\mu_m^{\otimes s-n})\to \\ H^{s-t}_{\text{\rm et}}(k(x)\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n})^G\to 0. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Niveau spectral sequence for etale homology with $\mathbb Z/m$ coefficients, with Hochschild-Serre descent sequences for $E^1$ terms.

nodes.name: Etale niveau spectral sequence
nodes.statement: \tilde E^1_{s,t}=\bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-t}_{\text{\rm et}}(k(x),\mu_m^{\otimes s-n}) \Rightarrow H_{s+t}^{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))
nodes.label: polk

nodes.name: Galois descent sequence mod m

nodes.name: Motivic, Frobenius and etale cohomology of fields mod m
nodes.statement: For $k$ a field of transcendence degree $s$ over ${{\mathbb F}}_q$ and $p\not|m$, $$H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n)) \cong H^{s-t}_{\text{\rm et}}(k,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n}) $$ for $t\geq n$. The left term vanishes for $t<n$, the middle term vanishes for $t<n-1$ and $$H^{s-n+1}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n))\cong H^{s-n}_{\mathcal M}(k\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n))_G \subseteq H^{s-n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(k,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n})$$ The right term vanishes for $t<-1$.
nodes.statement_short: For $p\nmid m$, motivic, Frobenius and etale cohomology of a field agree mod m for $t\ge n$, with vanishing ranges below.

nodes.statement: It suffices to show that the maps $$H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n))\to H^{s-t}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n)) \to H^{s-t}_{\text{\rm et}}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n))$$ are isomorphism for $t\geq n$. The total composition is an isomorphism by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures. Comparing the sequences \eqref{frobdescent} and \eqref{galoismodm}, it follows that the second map is an isomorphism by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures for the finite product of fields $k\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q$.

nodes.statement: It suffices to show that the maps $$H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n))\to H^{s-t}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n)) \to H^{s-t}_{\text{\rm et}}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n))$$ are isomorphism for $t\geq n$. The

nodes.name: Kato complex mod m
nodes.statement: We define $KC_n/m(X)$ to be the complex \begin{multline} \bigoplus_{X_{(n)}} {{\mathbb Z}}/m \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(n+1)}} H^1_{\text{\rm et}}(k(x)\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(1))_G \gets \cdots \\ \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-n}_{\text{\rm et}}(k(x)\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n))_G \gets\cdots, \end{multline} with the summand indexed by $X_{(s)}$ in degree $s-n$.

nodes.statement: We have $$H_i^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))\cong H_{i-2n}(KC_n/m(X)),$$ and theses groups vanish unless $2n\leq i\leq n+d$.
conclusions: $$H_i^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))\cong H_{i-2n}(KC_n/m(X)),$$

nodes.statement: Let ${{\mathbb Z}}(n)$ be Bloch's higher cycle complex indexed by codimension, so that ${{\mathbb Z}}(n)(X)^i=z^n(X,2n-i)$ and $H^{i}_{Zar}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))=CH_{d-n}(X,2n-i)$ is motivic cohomology for smooth $X$ of pure dimension $d$.

nodes.name: Frobenius and Kato cohomology
nodes.statement: If $X$ is smooth of pure dimension $d$, we set \begin{align} H^i_F(X,A(n))&=H_{2d+1-i}^F(X,A(d-n))\\ H^i_K(X,A(n))&=H_{2d-i}^K(X,A(d-n)). \end{align}

nodes.statement: The following are reformulations of Lemma \ref{lem1}:

nodes.name: Vanishing and descent for Frobenius and Kato cohomology
nodes.statement: The groups $H^i_F(X,A(n))$ vanish for $i>2n+1$, and in general there are short exact sequences $$ 0\to H^{i-1}_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,A(n))_G\to H^i_F(X,A(n))\to H^i_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,A(n))^G \to 0.$$ The groups $H^i_K(X,A(n))$ vanish for $i>2n$, and $$H^{2n}_K(X,A(n))\cong H^{2n+1}_F(X,A(n)) \cong \big(CH^n(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G.$$

nodes.name: Main comparison diagram
nodes.statement: We have a commutative diagram with exact rows \begin{equation}\begin{CD} @>>>{\bf H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))} @>\alpha >>{\bf H^i_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))} @>\beta>> {\bf H^{i-1}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))} @>\gamma>>\\ @EEE @Vf VV @Vg VV @VhVV \\ @>>> H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> {\bf H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) }@>>> H^{i-1}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))@>>> \end{CD}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Commutative diagram with exact rows comparing motivic-Frobenius-Kato with etale-Weil-etale-rational motivic cohomology.

nodes.name: Main diagram
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} @>>>{\bf H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))} @>\alpha >>{\bf H^i_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))} @>\beta>> {\bf H^{i-1}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))} @>\gamma>>\\ @EEE @Vf VV @Vg VV @VhVV \\ @>>> H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> {\bf H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) }@>>> H^{i-1}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))@>>> \end{CD}

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.2
nodes.statement: The upper row is exact by Proposition \ref{prop1}, and the lower row is the exact sequence relating etale cohomology to Weil-etale cohomology \cite{ichweilI}. The maps $f$ and $g$ are induced by the change of topology from the Zariski to the etale site.
nodes.statement_short: Upper row from Proposition 2.3, lower row from the Weil-etale sequence; vertical maps from change of topology.

nodes.name: Vertical maps are rational isomorphisms
nodes.statement: The vertical maps are isomorphisms after tensoring with ${{\mathbb Q}}$, because motivic cohomology and etale hypercohomology of the motivic complex agree with rational coefficients.

nodes.name: Finite generation conjecture (cohomological)
nodes.statement: The bold face terms are finitely generated for all $i,n$ and $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Motivic, Frobenius, Kato and Weil-etale cohomology groups of smooth proper X are finitely generated.
nodes.label: maincohom

nodes.name: Relation to Bass, Tate and Beilinson conjectures
nodes.statement: Finite generation of $H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is a generalization of Bass' conjecture, and finite generation of $H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is equivalent to Tate's and Beilinson's conjecture.

nodes.name: Lichtenbaum's conjecture
nodes.statement: The group $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is finite for all $i\not=2n,2n+1$, finitely generated for all $i=2n$, and of cofinite type for $i=2n+2$.
conclusions:
The group $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is finite for all $i\not=2n,2n+1$,
finitely generated for all $i=2n$, and of cofinite type for $i=2n+2$.
nodes.label: lichtconj

nodes.name: Kato cohomology in low degree
nodes.statement: The map $h:H^i_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$ is bijective for $i<n$ and injective for $i=n$.
conclusions: is bijective for $i<n$ and injective for $i=n$.
nodes.label: lowdegree

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement: By the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures, both the map $f$ as well as the map $g$ are isomorphism for $i\leq n+1$ and injective for $i=n+2$.
nodes.statement_short: Beilinson-Lichtenbaum makes f and g isomorphisms in low degrees; diagram chase.

nodes.name: Conjecture 3.3 for n=0
nodes.statement: Conjecture \ref{maincohom} holds for $n=0$.
conclusions: Conjecture \ref{maincohom} holds for $n=0$.

nodes.name: Computation for n=0
nodes.statement: In fact we have $H^i_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}})\cong H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}})\cong {{\mathbb Z}}$ for $i=0,1$, $H^0_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}})\cong H^0_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}})\cong {{\mathbb Z}}$, and all other homology groups vanish.
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation of all groups for weight 0.

nodes.name: The case n=1
nodes.statement: Let $n=1$. a) For $i=1$, the four left groups in \eqref{maind} are isomorphic to ${\mathcal O}_X(X)^\times$, and for $i=2$, they are isomorphic to $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$. b) The groups $H^i_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(1))$ vanish for $i\not=2$, and $H^2_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(1))\cong \operatorname{NS}(\bar X)_G$. c) For $i=3$, \begin{align*} H^3_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(1))&=0\\ H^3_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(1))&\cong \operatorname{Br}(X)\\ H^3_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(1))&\cong \operatorname{NS}(\bar X)_G, \end{align*} and $H^3_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(1))$ is an extension of $Br(\bar X)^G$ by $NS(\bar X)_G$. d) All groups in \eqref{maind} are finitely generated, except possibly $H^3_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(1))\cong \operatorname{Br}(X)$ and $H^3_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(1))$, whose finiteness is equivalent to Tate's conjecture for divisors.
nodes.statement_short: For weight 1 the groups are units, Picard, Neron-Severi coinvariants and Brauer groups; finite generation reduces to Tate for divisors.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.6
nodes.statement: This follows from ${{\mathbb Z}}(1)\cong {\mathbb G}_m[-1]$, Lemma \ref{plm} and $(\operatorname{Pic}^0 \bar X)_G =0$.
nodes.statement_short: Use $\mathbb Z(1)\cong\mathbb G_m[-1]$, Lemma 3.1 and vanishing of $(\mathrm{Pic}^0\bar X)_G$.

nodes.name: Kato cohomology of weight 2 in low degrees
nodes.statement: According to Parshin's conjecture and Lemma \ref{lowdegree}, the groups $H^i_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$ vanish for $i\leq 2$, and $H^4_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))\cong CH^2(\bar X)_G$.
conclusions:
the groups $H^i_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$ vanish for $i\leq 2$,
and $H^4_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))\cong CH^2(\bar X)_G$.

nodes.name: Maps $\epsilon$ and $\tau$
nodes.statement: To describe the remaining group, let $\epsilon:X_{{\text{\rm et}}}\to X_{{\text{\rm Zar}}}$ be the canonical map of sites, and $\tau$ the composition of the boundary map in the lower row of \eqref{maind} with the composition $$H^4_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))\to H^0(X,R^4\epsilon_*{{\mathbb Z}}(2))\cong H^0(X,R^3\epsilon_*{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(2)) =H^3_{nr}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(2)).$$
nodes.statement_short: $\epsilon$ is the change-of-sites map; $\tau$ composes the boundary map with the map to unramified cohomology.

nodes.name: Unramified cohomology
nodes.statement: The last term is known under the name unramified cohomology.

nodes.name: Torsion of $H^3_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$ via unramified cohomology
nodes.statement: The group ${}_{\text{\rm tor}} H^3_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$ is isomorphic to the cohomology of the sequence $$ H^2_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(2))\stackrel{\tau}{\to} H^3_{nr}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(2))\to H^3_{nr}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(2))^G.$$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.7
nodes.statement: The first statement follows from a diagram chase in \eqref{maind}, noting that due to the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjecture the maps $f$ and $g$ are injective, $\operatorname{coker} f=H^0(X,R^4\epsilon_*{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$ and $$\operatorname{coker} g= \operatorname{coker}\big( H^4_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))^G\to H^4_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))^G\big) \subseteq H^0(\bar X,R^4\epsilon_*{{\mathbb Z}}(2))^G.$$
nodes.statement_short: Diagram chase in the main diagram, with Beilinson-Lichtenbaum giving injectivity of f, g and computing their cokernels.

nodes.name: Kato cohomology $H^3_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$ and unramified cohomology
nodes.statement: Under Parshin's conjecture there is an exact sequence $$0\to H^3_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))\to H^3_{nr}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(2))\to H^3_{nr}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Q}},{{\mathbb Z}}(2))^G .$$ Thus ${}_{\text{\rm tor}} H^3_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$ consists of those elements in the cokernel of the integral cyle map, whose pull back to the algebraic closure $H^4_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$ lie in the image of the cycle map $CH^n(\bar X)\to H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.8
nodes.statement: Under Parshin's conjecture, $H^3_k(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$ is torsion. Furthermore, $\operatorname{coker} f$ is the obstruction to the integral Tate conjecture, and $\operatorname{coker} g$ is the cokernel of the map $CH^2(\bar X)^G\to H^4_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))^G$.
nodes.statement_short: Parshin makes $H^3_K$ torsion; identify coker f and coker g with integral Tate obstructions.

nodes.name: Geometrically rational X
nodes.statement: If $X$ is geometrically rational, then there are isomorphisms $H^3_{nr}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(2))\cong H^3_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$.
conclusions: $H^3_{nr}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(2))\cong H^3_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.9
nodes.statement: For rational $Z$ over a field $k$, we have $H^3_{nr}(Z,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(2))=H^3_{\text{\rm et}}(k,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$, and $H^2_{\mathcal M}(Z,{{\mathbb Q}}(2))\cong H^0(Z,{\mathcal H}^2({{\mathbb Q}}(2)))\cong H^2_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Q}}(2)) $ by \cite[2.1.9]{cothe}, and for $k$ the algebraic closure of a finite field these groups vanish.
nodes.statement_short: For rational varieties unramified and weight-2 rational motivic cohomology come from the base field, which vanish over $\bar{\mathbb F}_q$.

nodes.name: Pirutka's example
nodes.statement: Pirutka \cite{pirutka} constructed an element in $H^3_{nr}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/2)$ for $X$ a geometrically birational variety of dimension $5$, giving a non-trivial $2$-torsion element in $H^3_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(2))$.
nodes.statement_short: Pirutka's unramified class gives a nontrivial 2-torsion element of $H^3_K(X,\mathbb Z(2))$.

nodes.name: Top weight case
nodes.statement: If $n=\dim X$, then Conjecture \ref{maincohom} is equivalent to conjecture $P_0$. In this case, $H^i_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))=0$ for $i\not=2n$, and $H^{2n}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\cong {{\mathbb Z}}^{\pi_0(X)}$.
conclusions:
Conjecture \ref{maincohom} is equivalent to 
conjecture $P_0$.

nodes.name: Cohomological Parshin conjecture $P^n$
nodes.statement: The cohomological Parshin conjecture $P^n$ of \cite{parshinneu} states that $H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))=0$ for smooth and proper $X$ and $i\not=2n$.
conclusions: $H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))=0$

nodes.name: Parshin's conjecture and Weil-etale cohomology
nodes.statement: This is equivalent to isomorphisms $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) \cong H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ for $i\leq 2n$, and injectivity in degree $2n+1$ by \cite{ichweilI}.
nodes.statement_short: $P^n$ is equivalent to etale and Weil-etale cohomology agreeing up to degree $2n$ and injecting in degree $2n+1$.

nodes.name: Parshin's conjecture forces Kato cohomology to vanish in low degrees
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lowdegree}, Parshin's conjecture implies that the groups $H^i_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ vanish for $i\leq n$ if $n>0$, and that they torsion for $i\leq 2n$.
conclusions:
the groups 
$H^i_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ vanish for $i\leq n$ if $n>0$

nodes.name: Kato cohomology measures failure of integral Tate conjecture
nodes.statement: Diagram \eqref{maind} for $i<2n$ becomes \begin{equation} \begin{CD} @>>> H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> H^i_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> H^{i-1}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to \cdots \\ @III @VVV @VVV \\ @EEE H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @= H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) \end{CD}\end{equation} In degree $2n+1$ we get $$\begin{CD} 0@>>> CH^n(\bar X)_\varphi @= H^{2n}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> 0 \\ @VVV @VVV @VVV @VVV \\ H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>inj >> H^{2n+1}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>>> CH^n(X)_{{\mathbb Q}} @>>> H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) \end{CD}$$ The cokernel of the lower right horizontal map is the (conjecturally finite) group $H^{2n+2}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$. In degree $2n$ we have \begin{equation} \begin{CD} H^{2n-2}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>>> CH^n(X) @>\alpha >> H^{2n}_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> H^{2n-1}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to 0\\ @III @Vf VV @Vg VV \\ @EEE H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @= H^{2n}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) \end{CD}\end{equation} We get an exact sequence $$H^{2n-2}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to \ker f\to \ker g\to H^{2n-1}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) \to \operatorname{coker} f\to \operatorname{coker} g \to 0.$$ By Corollary \ref{tatecor} below, $f$ has conjecturally the same kernel and cokernel as the cycle map, whereas $g$ is related to the cycle map over the algebraic closure: $$ \begin{CD} 0@>>> H^{2n-1}_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))_G @>>> H^{2n}_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>>> CH^n(\bar X)^G @>>> 0\\ @III @VVV @Vg VV @VVV \\ 0@>>> H^{2n-1}_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))_G @>>> H^{2n}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>>> H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))^G @>>> 0 \end{CD}$$ Thus Kato homology measures the difference of the failure of the integral Tate conjecture over ${{\mathbb F}}_q$ and over its algebraic closure.
nodes.statement_short: Under Parshin, the main diagram degenerates and Kato cohomology measures the difference between integral Tate failures over $\mathbb F_q$ and $\bar{\mathbb F}_q$.

nodes.name: Diagram for i<2n
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} @>>> H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> H^i_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> H^{i-1}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to \cdots \\ @III @VVV @VVV \\ @EEE H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @= H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) \end{CD}

nodes.name: Diagram in degree 2n
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} H^{2n-2}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>>> CH^n(X) @>\alpha >> H^{2n}_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> H^{2n-1}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to 0\\ @III @Vf VV @Vg VV \\ @EEE H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @= H^{2n}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) \end{CD}

nodes.name: Localization for etale cohomology with $\mu_m^{\otimes n}$
nodes.statement: Assume that $p\not|m$. By the proper base change theorem, $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))$ is finite, and replacing ${{\mathbb Z}}/m(n)$ by $\mu_m^{\otimes n}$, we have a localization long exact sequence (the difference is that the latter is non-trivial for negative $n$).

nodes.name: Finiteness of motivic cohomology mod m over $\bar X$
nodes.statement: The question is if $H^i_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))$ is finite.

nodes.name: Schoen's examples
nodes.statement: There are examples of Schoen showing that for certain threefolds over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, the group $CH^2(\bar X)/l$ is not finite, which implies that $H^4_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}/l(2))$ cannot be finite.
nodes.section: 4 The algebraic closure of a finite field
nodes.statement_short: Some threefolds in characteristic 0 have infinite $CH^2/l$, so motivic cohomology mod l over $\bar X$ need not be finite.

nodes.name: Finiteness via the Bott element
nodes.statement: For $N\geq i$, consider the following diagram $$\begin{CD} H^i_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n)) @>>> H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,\mu_m^{\otimes n})\\ @V\cup \beta^{N-n} VV @| \\ H^i_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(N)) @= H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,\mu_m^{\otimes N}). \end{CD}$$ The lower row is an isomorphism by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjecture, and finiteness of $H^i_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))$ is equivalent to finiteness of the kernel of the cup-product with the Bott-element.
nodes.section: 4 The algebraic closure of a finite field
nodes.statement_short: Finiteness of motivic cohomology mod m of $\bar X$ is equivalent to finiteness of the kernel of cup product with the Bott element.

nodes.name: No localization for p-adic etale cohomology
nodes.statement: If $p=\operatorname{char} k$, then $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}/p(n))$ has no localization long exact sequence.
nodes.section: 4 The algebraic closure of a finite field

nodes.name: Brauer group of a supersingular abelian surface
nodes.statement: The groups $H^2_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}/p(1))$ and $H^3_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}/p(1))$ both contain the non-divisible $p$-torsion of the Brauer group $H^3(\bar X_{\text{\rm et}},{{\mathbb Z}}(1))$. For a supersingular abelian surface, this group contains the field $\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q$, hence is not finitely generated (however, its Galois invariants and coinvariants are finite).
nodes.section: 4 The algebraic closure of a finite field
nodes.statement_short: p-cohomology over $\bar X$ contains the non-divisible p-torsion of the Brauer group, which is not finitely generated for supersingular abelian surfaces.

nodes.name: Milne's duality for unipotent parts
nodes.statement: According to Milne, the unipotent part of $H^i(X_{\text{\rm et}},{{\mathbb Z}}/p(n))$ and $H^{2d+1-i}(X_{\text{\rm et}},{{\mathbb Z}}/p(d-n))$ are in duality.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence for p-coefficients
nodes.statement: There is a long exact sequence $$\cdots \to H^i_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}/p(n)) \to H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}/p(n)) \to H^{i-1-n}_{\text{\rm Zar}}(\bar X,R^1\epsilon_* \nu^n)\to\cdots .$$

nodes.statement_short: Long exact sequence linking motivic and etale cohomology mod p over $\bar X$ via $R^1\epsilon_*\nu^n$.

u^n)$ is infinite for $j

nodes.name: Integral structure of motivic cohomology over $\bar X$
nodes.statement: Regarding the integral structure of motivic cohomology, it is an interesting question if there is a presentation of the form $$ H^i_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\cong {{\mathbb Z}}^r\oplus ({{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}')^c\oplus ({{\mathbb Q}}_p/{{\mathbb Z}}_p)^{c_p} \oplus (\text{finite})$$ with $r=0$ unless $i=2n$.

nodes.statement_short: Is motivic cohomology over $\bar X$ a sum of a lattice, divisible groups and a finite group, with lattice only in degree 2n?

nodes.name: Lichtenbaum, Weil-etale finite generation and Parshin
nodes.statement: Fix an integer $n$ and a scheme $X$, and consider the following statements: \begin{enumerate} \item Lichtenbaum's conjecture \ref{lichtconj}. \item The groups $H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ are finitely generated. \item Parshin's conjecture. \end{enumerate} Then $a)\Leftrightarrow b) \Rightarrow c)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lichtenbaum's conjecture is equivalent to finite generation of Weil-etale cohomology, and both imply Parshin's conjecture.
conclusions: Then $a)\Leftrightarrow b) \Rightarrow c)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.1
nodes.statement: $a)\Rightarrow c)$ This follows because $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\cong H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$, and the former vanishes for $i\not=2n$ by hypothesis. To show the equivalence of a) and b) we can assume Parshin's conjecture, and consider the exact sequence of \cite{ichweilI} $$ \cdots \to H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{i-1}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\to \cdots.$$ Then a) and b) imply each other for $i\leq 2n$ and $i>2n+2$, and we are left with \begin{multline*} 0\to H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{2n+1}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\\ \to H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{2n+2}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to 0 . \end{multline*} By the Weil-conjectures and counting coranks one sees that the corank $C$ of $H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\cong H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ and of $H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ agree. a) $\Rightarrow$ b): Finiteness of $H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ implies that $C$ agrees with the dimension of $H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$, and since $H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is torsion, $H^{2n+1}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))/{\text{\rm tor}}$ must be a lattice of the same rank. Moreover $H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$ surjects onto the divisible part of $H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$, hence $H^{2n+2}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is finite. b) $\Rightarrow$ a) We see that $H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is finite, because $H^{2n+1}_W(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\cong H^{2n}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$ \cite{ichweilI}. For the same reason, $H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is an extension of the finite group $H^{2n+2}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ and a torsion divisible group of finite corank.
nodes.statement_short: a)$\Rightarrow$c) by rational comparison; a)$\Leftrightarrow$b) under Parshin via the etale/Weil-etale sequence. The key step is a corank count from the Weil conjectures in degrees $2n+1,2n+2$.

nodes.statement: $a)\Rightarrow c)$ This follows because $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\cong H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$, and the former vanishes for $i\not=2n$ by hypothesis.
nodes.statement_short: Rational etale and motivic cohomology agree, so Lichtenbaum gives Parshin.

nodes.statement: Then a) and b) imply each other for $i\leq 2n$ and $i>2n+2$, and we are left with \begin{multline*} 0\to H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{2n+1}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\\ \to H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{2n+2}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to 0 . \end{multline*}

nodes.name: Corank count
nodes.statement: By the Weil-conjectures and counting coranks one sees that the corank $C$ of $H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\cong H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ and of $H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ agree.
nodes.statement_short: Weil conjectures give equal coranks.

nodes.name: a) implies b)
nodes.statement: a) $\Rightarrow$ b): Finiteness of $H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ implies that $C$ agrees with the dimension of $H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$, and since $H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is torsion, $H^{2n+1}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))/{\text{\rm tor}}$ must be a lattice of the same rank. Moreover $H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$ surjects onto the divisible part of $H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$, hence $H^{2n+2}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is finite. b)
nodes.statement_short: Show the Weil-etale groups in degrees $2n+1,2n+2$ are finitely generated.

nodes.name: b) implies a)
nodes.statement: b) $\Rightarrow$ a) We see that $H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is finite, because $H^{2n+1}_W(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\cong H^{2n}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$ \cite{ichweilI}. For the same reason, $H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is an extension of the finite group $H^{2n+2}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ and a torsion divisible group of finite corank.
nodes.statement_short: Recover finiteness of etale cohomology from Weil-etale finite generation.

nodes.name: Factorization $c=wvu$ of the $l$-adic cycle map
nodes.statement: Using the functorial identification ${{\mathbb Z}}/m(n)\cong \mu_m^{\otimes n}$ for $\operatorname{char} k\not| m$ of \cite{bkbl} and ${{\mathbb Z}}/p^r(n)\cong \nu_r^n[-n]$ of \cite{marcI}, the $l$-adic cycle map can be factored as follows: $$ c:H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \stackrel{u}{\to} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \stackrel{v}{\to} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))^{\wedge l} \stackrel{w}{\hookrightarrow} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n)).$$
nodes.statement_short: The l-adic cycle map factors through etale motivic cohomology, its l-adic completion, and continuous l-adic cohomology.

nodes.name: l-adic completion and l-adic cohomology notation
nodes.statement: Here we write $A^{\wedge l}$ for the $l$-adic completion, and $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))$ for the $l$-adic cohomology $\operatornamewithlimits{lim} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/l^r(n))$ to distinguish it from the hypercohomology of ${{\mathbb Z}}(n)\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l$.

nodes.name: Surjectivity of completion map
nodes.statement: The completion map $v$ is surjective.
conclusions: The completion map $v$ is surjective.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: The ${{\mathbb Z}}_l$-module $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))^{\wedge l}\subseteq H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))$ is finitely generated and the cokernel of $v$ is $l$-divsible by \cite[(4.2)]{jannsencont}, hence must be trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Cokernel of v is l-divisible and finitely generated, hence zero.

nodes.name: Kernel-cokernel sequence for the cycle map
nodes.statement: We have an exact sequence \begin{multline*} 0\to \ker u\to \ker c\to {\rm div}\; H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \\ \to \operatorname{coker} u\to \operatorname{coker} c\to T_lH^{i+1}(X_{\text{\rm et}},{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to 0. \end{multline*} The groups $\ker u$ and $\operatorname{coker} u$ are torsion.
conclusions: The groups $\ker u$ and $\operatorname{coker} u$ are torsion.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.3
nodes.statement: This is the kernel-cokernel sequence of the composition $c= (wv)\circ u$. The kernel of $wv$ is the kernel of $v$, which is the group of divisible elements of $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes {{\mathbb Z}}_l$. The cokernel of $wv$ is the Tate module $T_lH^{i+1}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$.
nodes.statement_short: Kernel-cokernel sequence of $c=(wv)\circ u$, identifying kernel and cokernel of $wv$.

nodes.statement: This is the kernel-cokernel sequence of the composition $c= (wv)\circ u$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the kernel-cokernel sequence to $c=(wv)\circ u$.

nodes.statement_short: Identify the kernel of $wv$ with the divisible elements.

nodes.name: Cokernel of wv
nodes.statement: The cokernel of $wv$ is the Tate module $T_lH^{i+1}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the cokernel of $wv$ with the Tate module.

nodes.name: Cycle map and change of topology
nodes.statement: Under Conjecture \ref{lichtconj}, the kernel and cokernel of $u$ are equal to the kernel and cokernel of the cycle map, respectively.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.4
nodes.statement: If $i\not=2n$, then all groups in the factorization of $c$ are expected to be finite, and $v$ and $w$ are isomorphisms. The cycle map $CH^n(X)\otimes {{\mathbb Z}}_l\to H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))$ is rationally surjective if and only if $T_lH^{i+1}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ vanishes, hence Tate's conjecture is equivalent to $\operatorname{Div} H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ torsion free. It is rationally injective (Beilinson's conjecture) if and only if $\operatorname{div} H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is torsion.
nodes.statement_short: For $i\ne 2n$ all groups are finite; in degree $2n$ relate Tate and Beilinson conjectures to divisible parts of etale cohomology.

nodes.name: Case i not 2n
nodes.statement: If $i\not=2n$, then all groups in the factorization of $c$ are expected to be finite, and $v$ and $w$ are isomorphisms.
nodes.statement_short: For $i\ne 2n$ all groups are finite and v, w are isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Rational surjectivity and Tate
nodes.statement: The cycle map $CH^n(X)\otimes {{\mathbb Z}}_l\to H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))$ is rationally surjective if and only if $T_lH^{i+1}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ vanishes, hence Tate's conjecture is equivalent to $\operatorname{Div} H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ torsion free.
nodes.statement_short: Relate rational surjectivity of the cycle map (Tate) to vanishing of the Tate module.

nodes.name: Rational injectivity and Beilinson
nodes.statement: It is rationally injective (Beilinson's conjecture) if and only if $\operatorname{div} H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is torsion.
nodes.statement_short: Relate rational injectivity (Beilinson) to torsion of the divisible part.

nodes.name: Short exact sequence coker r, coker u, ker s
nodes.statement: Considering the diagram $$\begin{CD} H^{2n-1}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>inj>> H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>>> H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n)) @>surj>> H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\\ @VrVV @VuVV @| @VsVV \\ H^{2n-1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>inj>> H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>>> H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n)) @>>> H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n)), \end{CD}$$ we obtain a short exact sequence $0\to \operatorname{coker} r\to \operatorname{coker} u\to \ker s\to 0$, and all three groups are conjecturally finite.
nodes.statement_short: A comparison diagram gives $0\to\mathrm{coker}\,r\to\mathrm{coker}\,u\to\ker s\to 0$.

nodes.name: Colimit over finite extensions
nodes.statement: Let $X_r=X\times_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}{{\mathbb F}}_{q^r}$, $G_r=Gal(\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q/{{\mathbb F}}_{q^r})$ and consider the colimit over the composition \begin{multline} H^i_{\mathcal M}(X_r,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \stackrel{u}{\to} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X_r,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \stackrel{v}{\twoheadrightarrow} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X_r,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))^{\wedge l} \stackrel{w}{\hookrightarrow}\\ H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X_r,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))\stackrel{x}{\twoheadrightarrow} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))^{G_r}. \end{multline}

nodes.name: Cycle map $\bar c$ over the algebraic closure
nodes.statement: It is clear that the first two groups commute with the colimit in $r$, so if we write $\gamma_*M=\operatornamewithlimits{colim} M^{G_r}$ for the largest continuous submodule of a Galois-module, then the colimit takes the form \begin{multline} \bar c: H^i_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \stackrel{\bar u}{\to} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \stackrel{\bar v}{\twoheadrightarrow} \operatornamewithlimits{colim} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X_r,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))^{\wedge l} \stackrel{\bar w}{\hookrightarrow}\\ \operatornamewithlimits{colim} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X_r,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))\twoheadrightarrow \gamma_* H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n)). \end{multline}

nodes.statement_short: With $\gamma_*M$ the largest continuous submodule, the colimit gives the factorization of $\bar c$.

nodes.name: Surjection not an isomorphism
nodes.statement: Note that surjectivity of $v$ implies that $\operatornamewithlimits{colim} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X_r,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))^{\wedge l}$ surjects onto $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))^{\wedge l}$, but the example of $\operatorname{Br}(X)=H^3_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(1))$ shows that this surjection is not an isomorphism in general.
